newsitem.title: UK: Brit Biotech shares calm amid MGAM storm.
newsitem.headline: Brit Biotech shares calm amid MGAM storm.

text.p: Investors in British Biotech Plc, the fast-growing drug discovery group, are reacting calmly to the storm surrounding its biggest shareholder, Morgan Grenfell Asset Management MGAM, analysts said on Thursday.
MGAM, which saw three of its investment funds suspended this week amid a regulatory investigation, had an 11.34 percent stake in the group on July 23, the last date it declared its interest.

Market-makers said early fears that British Biotech shares could flood onto the market if the funds were forced to liquidate holdings have largely subsided, with the company's shares holding fairly steady so far this week.

One analyst who asked not to be named said "there is no particular nervousness around the stock. There was a knee-jerk reaction at the start on Monday as people made the connection, but it has steadied up."

Shares in British Biotech, which has ridden high this year on hopes for its ground-breaking anti-cancer drug Marimastat, recovered from opening weakness on Monday when news of MGAM's troubles broke to close the day 3 1/2 pence higher at 221. The stock closed 7 pence lower at 215 pence on Thursday.
Another analyst, who also declined to be identified, said however that a lack of information about MGAM's intentions is worrying some investors.
"The basic situation is that we don't know what is going to happen," she said. "I think there probably is some nervousness among holders that we talk to, but that hasn't come to them selling shares."
She noted that the share price has held up this week in the face of high volume trading, with three million shares changing hands on Wednesday and 8-1/2 million on Tuesday.
"The fact that they have held up quite well is quite an enouraging sign. It suggests there has been real buying interest there."

Analysts said news that MGAM's owner Deutsche Bank AG has injected 180 million into the funds, which resumed trading on Thursday, has also provided reassurance. British Biotech repesented more than six percent of the portfolio of the largest of the three funds, MG European Growth, at the end of May and was by far its biggest UK investment.
A spokeswoman for British Biotech said the problems at MGAM were not a particular cause for concern, and noted that the stakes were spread across several funds.
She said that the relatively high turnover in the stock shows there are "plenty of buyers around."
